svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling instance refresh. A refresh replaces the instances in a group with ones built from a desired configuration, using either the default rolling strategy, which terminates instances and launches new ones in batches, or the replace root volume strategy, which updates only the root volume without terminating the instance and so preserves network interfaces, non-root EBS volumes and instance store data. Three settings have different defaults depending on whether the refresh is started from the console or from the CLI or an SDK, and the difference changes the failure mode. Skip matching is disabled in the CLI and SDK but enabled in the console; scale-in protected instances default to Wait in the CLI and SDK but Ignore in the console; and standby instances likewise default to Wait in the CLI and SDK but Ignore in the console. Wait means Auto Scaling waits one hour for you to act and the instance refresh fails if you do not, whereas Ignore means those instances are simply left alone and keep the old configuration. So the same operation either fails loudly after an hour or silently skips instances, depending on the door you came through. Skip matching carries its own trap: it compares each instance's current AMI ID against the AMI IDs in the desired configuration and only replaces instances where they do not match, but it does not check for code changes deployed from a user data script, and AWS recommends turning it off if user data pulls new code so that all instances receive the latest code even without a launch template version update. The rollback constraints are the sharpest finding. The rollback option is only available if you specify a desired configuration when starting the refresh; you can only roll back to a previous version of a launch template if the version is a specific numbered version; and the rollback option is not available if the Auto Scaling group is configured to use the dollar-Latest or dollar-Default launch template version, nor can you roll back to a launch template configured to use an AMI alias from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. A group pinned to dollar-Latest therefore rolls forward onto whatever version exists with no supported way back. Auto rollback is disabled by default in both the console and the CLI, and if you specify a CloudWatch alarm but do not enable auto rollback and the alarm goes into the ALARM state, the instance refresh fails without rolling back. Other defaults: minimum healthy percentage is 90 percent when there is no instance maintenance policy, maximum healthy percentage is 100 percent, the difference between them cannot be greater than 100, bake time is zero, checkpoints are disabled with a checkpoint delay of one hour, and instance warmup falls back to the default instance warmup if defined or the health check grace period otherwise. Setting both minimum and maximum healthy percentage to 100 percent replaces one instance at a time and launches before terminating; a minimum of 0 percent replaces all instances at once. Timing limits: a refresh can actively replace instances for a maximum of 14 days, and when it cannot continue because it is waiting on standby or protected instances or because new instances fail health checks, Auto Scaling keeps retrying for an hour before the operation fails. During a refresh, a scale-out event launches new instances with the desired configuration rather than the group's current settings, InService instances are replaced before warm pool instances, and the group's settings are updated to the desired configuration only after the refresh succeeds. Attribute-based instance selection does not support SkipMatching or DesiredConfiguration and a refresh started with either will fail.
svg.title: On $Latest there is no way back from an instance refresh
svg.text: The convenience that removes your rollback.
“The rollback option is not available if the Auto Scaling group is configured to use the $Latest or
$Default launch template version.”
Three defaults that differ by door — and invert the failure mode
CLI / SDK console
Skip matching disabled ENABLED
Scale-in protected instances Wait Ignore
Standby instances Wait Ignore
Wait = fail after an hour. Ignore = leave them on the old config, quietly.
Skip matching compares AMI IDs, not your code
“Skip matching doesn’t check for code changes that are deployed from a user data script.”
So a console refresh on an unchanged template skips the very instances you meant to update.
AWS recommends turning it off when user data pulls new code.
ROLLBACK NEEDS ALL OF THIS
A desired configuration specified at start
A specific numbered template version
NOT $Latest, NOT $Default
No SSM Parameter Store AMI alias
And only while the refresh is still running.
AUTO ROLLBACK IS OFF BY DEFAULT
In the console and the CLI alike
An alarm without auto rollback fails the
refresh “without rolling back”
Max 10 alarms, and none may start in
ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA
The pacing defaults
min healthy 90% · max healthy 100% · bake time 0 · checkpoint delay 1 hour
warmup = default instance warmup, else the health check grace period
Both percentages at 100 replaces one at a time and launches before terminating. A minimum of 0 replaces all at once.
A refresh may actively replace for up to 14 days, and retries for one hour when it cannot continue before failing.
Mid-refresh scale-out launches with the desired configuration, and InService instances are replaced before warm pool ones.
Attribute-based instance selection supports neither SkipMatching nor DesiredConfiguration — the refresh fails outright.
